```{r setup}
results_dir <- Sys.getenv("KAPPA_SMALL_N_RESULTS_DIR", unset = "results")
required <- file.path(results_dir, c("summary.csv", "diagnostics.csv", "metadata.csv"))
missing <- required[!file.exists(required)]
if (length(missing) > 0L) {
  stop("Missing experiment results. Run `Rscript run_experiment.R --reps 2000 --progress` first.")
}
summary <- read.csv(required[[1L]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
diagnostics <- read.csv(required[[2L]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
metadata_raw <- read.csv(required[[3L]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
metadata <- setNames(metadata_raw$value, metadata_raw$key)

fmt <- function(x, digits = 3L) formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")
fmt_int <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 0L, format = "f", big.mark = ",")
method_order <- c("wald_z", "wald_fisher", "profile_lr", "profile_lr_robust",
                  "score_normal", "score_robust", "score_robust_t",
                  "moment_profile", "moment_profile_f")
summary <- summary[order(summary$n, match(summary$method, method_order)), ]
```

## Question

Can profile-likelihood or score inversion improve confidence-interval coverage
for quadratic Fleiss kappa when the number of subjects is only 20 or 30?

The experiment deliberately studies one difficult cell: five exchangeable
raters, five uniformly distributed ordered categories, true quadratic Fleiss
kappa `r fmt(as.numeric(metadata[["target"]]), 2)`, and complete data. It feeds
the quadratic companion paper (Paper C) and is an interval-method probe, not a
new estimator comparison.

## Short Answer

```{r short-answer}
best <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(summary, summary$n), function(d) {
  d[which.min(abs(d$coverage - 0.95)), ]
}))
wald <- subset(summary, method == "wald_z")
best_text <- paste(sprintf(
  "at n = %d, %s covers %s (Wald: %s)",
  best$n, best$method_label, fmt(best$coverage, 3), fmt(wald$coverage, 3)
), collapse = "; ")
cell_value <- function(method, n, column) {
  summary[summary$method == method & summary$n == n, column][[1L]]
}
robust_text <- paste(sprintf(
  "n = %d: robust profile %s, robust score-t %s, moment profile-F %s",
  c(20L, 30L),
  fmt(vapply(c(20L, 30L), function(n) cell_value("profile_lr_robust", n, "coverage"), numeric(1)), 3),
  fmt(vapply(c(20L, 30L), function(n) cell_value("score_robust_t", n, "coverage"), numeric(1)), 3),
  fmt(vapply(c(20L, 30L), function(n) cell_value("moment_profile_f", n, "coverage"), numeric(1)), 3)
), collapse = "; ")
se_rows <- unique(summary[, c("n", "se_ratio")])
se_text <- paste(sprintf("n = %d: %s", se_rows$n, fmt(se_rows$se_ratio, 3)),
                 collapse = "; ")
```

The magmaan-inspired methods are feasible, but “robust” and “small-sample” are
not synonyms. The robust sandwich rescales a misspecified normal working
criterion; by itself it remains a first-order chi-square approximation. In
this run, `r best_text`. None of the robust inversions is close to 0.95:
`r robust_text`. The IF mean SE / empirical SD ratios are `r se_text`, so the
central problem is small-sample variance underestimation plus an exact-agreement
boundary mass, not merely a poor choice of scale. The direct robust moment
profile tests whether profiling the three Fleiss moments helps without relying
on normality. The `t(n-3)` / `F(1,n-3)` rows add an explicit, clearly labelled
finite-sample critical-value heuristic.

This is a screening experiment. A method is promising only if it improves both
sample sizes without excessive length or numerical failures.

## Evidence

```{r evidence-table}
tab <- data.frame(
  `n` = summary$n,
  Method = summary$method_label,
  Coverage = fmt(summary$coverage, 3),
  `Valid-Only Coverage` = fmt(summary$coverage_valid, 3),
  `MC SE` = fmt(summary$coverage_mcse, 3),
  `Miss Below` = fmt(summary$miss_below, 3),
  `Miss Above` = fmt(summary$miss_above, 3),
  `Mean Length` = fmt(summary$mean_length, 3),
  Failures = summary$failures,
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(tab, align = "rlrrrrrrr")
```

Coverage counts an unavailable interval as not covering; `Valid-Only Coverage`
conditions on a returned interval, and `Failures` shows the difference. All
methods use the same Fleiss point estimate. The repeated estimate-level
columns in `results/replicates.csv` make it possible to diagnose interval misses
without rerunning the simulation.

```{r calibration-table}
cal <- unique(summary[, c("n", "bias", "empirical_sd", "mean_se", "se_ratio")])
cal <- cal[order(cal$n), ]
cal_tab <- data.frame(
  `n` = cal$n,
  Bias = fmt(cal$bias, 4),
  `Empirical SD` = fmt(cal$empirical_sd, 4),
  `Mean IF SE` = fmt(cal$mean_se, 4),
  `SE / SD` = fmt(cal$se_ratio, 3),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(cal_tab, align = "rrrrr")
```

## Methods

For subject \(i\), let \(m_i\) be the mean score, \(q_i\) the mean squared
score, and \(d_i\) the mean squared difference over rater pairs. Quadratic
Fleiss kappa is the smooth three-moment functional

\[
  \kappa_F = 1 - \frac{\bar d}{2(\bar q - \bar m^2)}.
\]

The ordinary and Fisher rows use the influence-function covariance returned by
`kappa_counts(estimator = "fleiss_cuzick", weight = "quadratic")`. The robust
moment profile minimizes the fixed-weight empirical GMM distance from
\((\bar m,\bar q,\bar d)\) subject to a candidate value of \(\kappa_F\), using the
empirical covariance of the three subject moments.

The other profile and score rows use the working model

\[
  Y_i \sim N\{\mu 1,\;\tau^2[(1-\kappa)I + \kappa J]\}.
\]

In this complete exchangeable design, its unrestricted pseudo-MLE for
\(\kappa\) equals the quadratic Fleiss moment estimate. The profile LR and
ordinary score use normal information. Their robust variants use the empirical
variance of the nuisance-orthogonal casewise score; the robust LR is divided by
the resulting one-direction sandwich scale. This is the scalar counterpart of
magmaan's robust score and robust profile-LRT scaling. The `t(n-3)` score and
`F(1,n-3)` moment profile are finite-sample heuristics, not established exact
reference distributions.

```{r diagnostics-table}
diag_tab <- data.frame(
  `n` = diagnostics$n,
  `Max |Package - Moment Estimate|` = format(diagnostics$max_abs_package_delta_estimate,
                                             scientific = TRUE, digits = 2),
  `Max |Package - Moment SE|` = format(diagnostics$max_abs_package_delta_se,
                                       scientific = TRUE, digits = 2),
  `Minimum GMM Rank` = diagnostics$min_gmm_rank,
  `Median Robust LR Scale` = fmt(diagnostics$median_cs_scale, 3),
  `Median Seconds / Replicate` = fmt(diagnostics$median_seconds_per_replicate, 3),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(diag_tab, align = "rrrrrr")
```

The equality diagnostics are deliberate: they ensure that any coverage change
comes from test inversion rather than silently switching estimands or point
estimators.

## Caveats

The data are complete, raters are exchangeable, and the marginal category
distribution is uniform. Results do not yet transfer to missing ratings,
non-exchangeable raters, alpha, or lower-agreement regimes. The normal working
model is intentionally false for these categorical observations, although its
first two moments are correct. The GMM covariance is estimated once at the
unrestricted empirical moments; continuously updated GMM and empirical
likelihood remain possible follow-ups.

Earlier archived experiments already found that one-term Edgeworth corrections,
generic bootstrap intervals, smooth second-order delta corrections, and simple
rare-disagreement hurdle intervals were not convincing general defaults. They
are not repeated here.

## Reproduce

```{r reproduce-table}
run_tab <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Replications per n", "Sample sizes", "Raters", "Categories",
               "True kappa", "Knowledge probability", "Seed base",
               "misskappa version", "Elapsed seconds"),
  Value = c(metadata[["reps"]], metadata[["n_grid"]], metadata[["raters"]],
            metadata[["categories"]], metadata[["target"]],
            fmt(as.numeric(metadata[["knowledge_probability"]]), 6),
            metadata[["seed_base"]], metadata[["misskappa_version"]],
            fmt(as.numeric(metadata[["elapsed_seconds"]]), 1)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(run_tab, align = "ll")
```

From this directory:

```bash
Rscript run_experiment.R --smoke --progress
Rscript run_experiment.R --reps 2000 --cores 4 --progress
quarto render report.qmd
```

The report reads summaries only. Set `KAPPA_SMALL_N_RESULTS_DIR` to render
against another compatible result directory.
